content.value_statement: Azure authentication choices vary across local development and hosted workloads. This skill provides focused Azure Identity patterns for secure .NET client configuration.
actual_capabilities: Recommends Azure.Identity packages for standard, dependency injection, and brokered authentication scenarios.
Explains DefaultAzureCredential order and customization options for development and production.
Provides .NET patterns for managed identity, service principals, certificates, and developer credentials.
Shows Azure client integration for Blob Storage and Key Vault.
Covers sovereign cloud authorities, retry options, logging, exception handling, and credential reuse.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples but does not execute authentication or verify Azure resources.
Uses placeholder tenant, client, secret, certificate, and endpoint values that users must replace securely.
Version references can become outdated as Azure.Identity packages change.
Does not configure Microsoft Entra applications, role assignments, managed identities, or network access.

use_cases.title: Local .NET Development
use_cases.description: Choose developer credentials and configure DefaultAzureCredential for an application that uses Azure SDK clients.

use_cases.title: Azure-Hosted Workloads
use_cases.description: Select managed identity patterns for App Service, Functions, virtual machines, or Azure Kubernetes Service.

use_cases.title: Enterprise Authentication Review
use_cases.description: Compare service principal, certificate, sovereign cloud, and deterministic production credential options.

prompt_templates.title: Install Azure Identity
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to add Azure.Identity to a .NET project and authenticate one BlobServiceClient with DefaultAzureCredential. Use placeholder endpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Development and Production
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a .NET approach that uses DefaultAzureCredential locally and managed identity in Azure. Explain the required configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Dependency Injection
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ASP.NET Core design for Blob Storage and Key Vault using Microsoft.Extensions.Azure. Reuse one credential and explain failure handling.
prompt_templates.scenario: Shared authentication for multiple Azure clients

prompt_templates.title: Review an Enterprise Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this .NET Azure authentication design: [describe environment]. Recommend deterministic credentials, sovereign cloud settings, retries, logging, and secret handling.

output_examples.input: Choose authentication for a .NET API running in Azure App Service and on developer laptops.
output: Development: use DefaultAzureCredential so approved developer tools can authenticate.
Production: use the App Service managed identity through ManagedIdentityCredential.
Reuse one credential instance and grant only required Azure roles.

output_examples.input: Review a service principal setup that stores a client secret in source control.
output_examples.output: The review rejects source-controlled secrets, recommends managed identity, and lists required role, deployment, rotation, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Explain why DefaultAzureCredential works locally but fails in an Azure workload.
output: Confirm which local developer credential succeeds.
Verify that the Azure resource has an enabled managed identity.
Check identity selection, role assignments, endpoint configuration, and authentication logs.

best_practices: Use managed identity or another deterministic credential in production.
Reuse credential instances across Azure SDK clients to improve token caching and connection behavior.
Keep secrets outside source control and limit diagnostic logging to approved environments.
anti_patterns: Do not embed client secrets, certificate passwords, or production credentials in prompts or source files.
Do not enable interactive browser authentication for unattended production services.
Do not rely on a broad credential chain in production when one credential type is known.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure.Identity packages, credential selection, Azure client integration, production guidance, retries, logging, and common authentication exceptions.

faq.question: Does the skill execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: The skill provides guidance. An agent may run package commands only when the task requires them and the environment permits execution.

faq.question: Which credential should production workloads use?
faq.answer: Use managed identity when available. Otherwise, select one deterministic credential that matches the deployment and secret-management requirements.

faq.question: How should client secrets and certificates be handled?
faq.answer: Keep them outside source control, restrict access, rotate them, and prefer managed identity when the Azure service supports it.

faq.question: Does the guidance support sovereign clouds?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies Azure authority hosts for public, government, China, and Germany environments.

faq.question: Can this skill verify that authentication works?
faq.answer: No. Users must test credentials, role assignments, endpoints, and network access in their own Azure environment.
